facts.fact: A Grease Pencil object's data in 4.5 is a GreasePencil from bpy.data.grease_pencils_v3 (layers -> frames -> drawing -> strokes), and the object's type is 'GREASEPENCIL'. The pre-4.3 types (bpy.data.grease_pencils, GPencilStroke) still exist, for annotations; code written for them does not draw Grease Pencil objects

Strokes are added with drawing.add_strokes(point_counts) and filled through attributes: 'position' (POINT) and, added when needed, 'radius' (POINT, in metres) and 'cyclic' (CURVE). A new drawing's attributes before any are added
A Grease Pencil material is a normal material given Grease Pencil settings with bpy.data.materials.create_gpencil_data(mat); its stroke colour is mat.grease_pencil.color
A Grease Pencil drawing renders headless in EEVEE, Cycles and Workbench (Grease Pencil is drawn as its own pass on top of the render); dark_fraction is the share of the 256 px frame the ink covers
object.grease_pencil_add(type='LINEART_SCENE') works headless and gives a Grease Pencil object with a Line Art modifier; the strokes it generates are read from the evaluated object

Freestyle (render.use_freestyle) draws lines on a Cycles render headless, but in a scene made from an empty factory file the view layer's line set has no line style: the render printed a Python error ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'use_chaining'), raised nothing, and came out without lines. With bpy.data.linestyles.new() assigned to the line set, lines appear (dark share of the white frame below)
